title: Wireless Power Transfer Performance for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Charging
content:
A selectively powered hexagonal transmitter array combined with a novel L-shaped pickup coil is proposed for UAV wireless charging. Finite element simulations show the design achieves higher uncompensated power and greater positional stability than a benchmark coil, offering a promising direction towards scalable, misalignment-tolerant charging platforms.


ABSTRACT

The growing adoption of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in delivery, surveillance, agriculture and photography necessitates efficient and scalable charging solutions. Conventional charging methods are time-consuming, labour-intensive and limit operational autonomy. Wireless power transfer (WPT) offers a promising alternative for multi-rotor UAV charging by enabling autonomous energy replenishment. This paper proposes a WPT scheme employing a horizontal magnetic field with an array of selectively powered hexagonal transmit coils and an L-shaped pickup coil. To evaluate performance, finite element analysis (FEA) simulations were conducted in Ansys Maxwell to investigate the magnetic coupling and uncompensated power transfer and optimal coil orientation at various positions on the charging platform. This is a simulation-only study; no physical prototype was built or tested. Results demonstrate that the proposed design mitigates alignment issues and shows higher uncompensated power (coupling strength) than the benchmark design under simulation, indicating a potentially scalable direction for UAV charging that would require hardware validation before practical deployment.
